events.text: There is no witness but the incense. {npc} kneels across from you, the stick burning between you, and says the old words that couples of the murim have said for a thousand years: one road, two walking it, and whoever reaches the top first waits. Then {he} adds, in {his} own voice: "And no going on alone. Promise."

effects.log: You promise. The incense burns down to the end in one unbroken line of ash, which the old books say is lucky.

choices.text: Promise to wait, not to never leave

effects.log: "I will wait," you say. "I cannot promise more than I know." {npc} thinks about it, and accepts the smaller true thing.

events.text: You swear the vow with {npc} in the courtyard, and by the time the incense is out the whole house knows. Supper is very quiet. Someone sets the dishes down a little too hard. {npc} reaches for your hand under the table and squeezes it once, which helps, and does not help at all.

effects.log: You say that a vow on the road takes nothing from the house. Nobody answers. But somebody passes the rice.
You eat in silence. Tomorrow will be easier, or it will not; tonight is for the vow.

events.text: You have both come a long way to this terrace: {npc} at {his} realm, you at yours, two masters the murim already speaks of. The vow between such people is not a sweet thing. It is a contract with heaven. Below you the clouds move, and somewhere above them is the road you have just sworn to walk together.

effects.log: You both look up. It is very far. For the first time it does not seem too far.

mem.note: was looked at instead of the sky

effects.log: You look at {npc} instead. {He} is already looking at you. The clouds can wait.

events.text: You come out of the breakthrough with the world sharper than before, and the first thing you feel is not your own power but {npc}'s: down the thread of the vow, {his} qi stirring in answer, like a second bell struck by the first.

effects.log: You find {npc} in the yard with {his} eyes closed, breathing the way you breathed an hour ago. You sit beside {him} and keep watch.
You sleep a day and a night. When you wake, {npc} has left a bowl of rice and a note: Felt it. Well done.

events.text: You break through, and a heartbeat later something in {npc} gives way too, a step behind you on the same stair. The two of you look at each other across the room with the same astonished face. The books say a vow is a thread. Nobody said it would pull.

effects.log: You both laugh, at nothing, at everything. The servants think you have gone mad. Perhaps you have.
You write down exactly what you felt. One day someone else will swear this vow and need to know.

events.text: {npc} breaks through in the night, and you wake before {he} does, sitting straight up in the dark with your heart pounding and your meridians full of someone else's light. It fades by morning. But you know a little more about the next step of the road than you did yesterday.

effects.log: {npc} listens with {his} chin in {his} hand. "So that is what it looks like from outside," {he} says.
You keep it to yourself. Some things are better as a secret you share without saying.

events.text: {npc} comes out of seclusion a realm above where {he} went in, and stands in the doorway blinking at the sunlight like someone who has slept a hundred years. Then {he} looks at you and says, slightly embarrassed: "I think I left a door open behind me. Come and see."

effects.log: You sit where {npc} sat. Something of the path is still in the air there, like warmth in a chair.
You make {npc} eat and sleep. The door stays open a little longer than it would have. That seems right.

events.text: The first form of your paired technique is nothing at all: you stand back to back with {npc} and learn to breathe at the same time. It takes all year. On the last day, a sparrow lands on your shoulder, then on {npc}'s, as if it cannot tell which of you is which.

effects.log: You keep breathing together long after the sparrow has gone. Neither of you wants to be the first to stop.
You call it the Sparrow's Mistake. {npc} groans. The name sticks anyway.

events.text: Halfway through the paired technique you stop being able to tell whose blade is whose. {npc} parries a strike aimed at you before you see it; you finish a cut {he} began. Your sparring partners refuse, after the third bout, to fight the two of you together.

effects.log: You enter a pair bout at the provincial meet and win it so quickly the judges ask you to do it again, slower.
You never show it in public. A technique that only two people know is a technique nobody can answer.

events.text: The paired technique is finished. You know it the way one knows a song is finished: there is nothing left to add. You and {npc} do it once more on the frozen lake, one circle of light between two blades, and the ice under you rings like a bell for a whole minute afterwards.

choices.text: Give it to a disciple one day

effects.log: You agree to teach it, one day, to a pair who deserve it. {npc} writes it down in two halves, one for each of you.
You agree it is yours and {npc}'s alone, and will go where you go. That makes it heavier and more precious.

events.text: A season in the dark with {npc}, the door sealed, one lamp between you. You do not speak for weeks. You do not need to. By the end you can feel the turn of {his} qi the way one feels the turn of a tide, and you come out into the daylight with your eyes watering and your heart very quiet.

effects.log: You train that same afternoon. Everything is a little easier, the way a road is easier the second time.
You sit on the step in the sun for a whole day, saying nothing. It is the best day of the year.

events.text: In the third month of the seclusion {npc} speaks, for the first time, very softly: a question about the Dao that you have been circling for ten years without daring to ask. Hearing it in someone else's voice, you suddenly know the answer. Then you are not sure. Then you know it again.

effects.log: You answer. {npc} is quiet for so long you think {he} has fallen asleep. Then: "Yes," {he} says. "That."
You do not answer. Some questions are better as company than as answers.

events.text: A seclusion above the clouds is a strange thing: no dark, no door, only a cloud sea that closes over you both like water and opens again a season later. {npc} comes out of it smiling at something {he} will not tell you, and you find you do not need to be told.

effects.log: You trust it. Up here, on this road, that is a kind of cultivation too.
"Later," {npc} says, "when you catch up." You laugh and chase {him} across the clouds.

events.text: In the dark of the seclusion your qi turns, all at once, like a river jumping its banks. You are drowning in your own meridians. Then {npc}'s palm is flat on your back, and {his} breath is setting the pace for yours, slow, slower, and the river goes back into its bed.

effects.log: "You would have done the same," {npc} says, and then, because {he} is honest: "I hope."
If your qi had pulled {him} in, you would both have died. "I know," {npc} says, and says nothing else.

events.text: The deviation is {npc}'s this time, not yours: in the lamp light you see {his} face go grey and {his} hands begin to shake. Every instinct says to stop, to run for a physician, to break the seclusion. You put your hand on {his} back instead.

effects.log: You hold steady through the night. In the morning {npc} opens {his} eyes and says your name, and you start breathing again.

choices.text: Break the seal and run for help

effects.log: You break the seal. The physician comes; {npc} lives. Later {he} asks, quietly, why you did not trust the vow.

events.text: A rumour comes to the house, the kind with a sharp end: {npc} was seen in the city with a stranger, at night, at a door with no sign. By the time {npc} comes home, three people have told you three versions of it. {He} sees your face and stops in the doorway.

effects.log: "A physician," {npc} says. "For a cough I did not want you to worry about." It is true. You are both ashamed, differently.
You say nothing. {npc} knows something is wrong and cannot find out what. A week of cold dinners follows.

events.text: {npc} has found a manual: half a technique of the old masters, the kind that could carry one of you a realm ahead and leave the other standing. There is only one copy. {He} sets it on the table between you and folds {his} hands, waiting to see what you will do.

effects.log: You push it across. {npc} looks at it a long time, then tears it carefully in two and hands you half. "We learn it together, or not at all."
You take it. {npc} says nothing. You learn it alone, and it is a good technique, and it tastes of ash.

events.text: On a ledge above a gorge, in a storm, the path gives way under {npc}. {He} catches the edge with one hand. You could reach {him}. You could also fall. There is perhaps a breath to decide in, and {npc} is looking at you, not at the drop.

effects.log: You reach. For one long moment you are both hanging over the gorge. Then you are both on the path, soaked, laughing like idiots.
"Climb!" you shout, and {npc} climbs, by {his} own strength, and does not look at you on the walk home.

events.text: An old enemy of yours offers {npc} a great deal of silver to tell them where you go to train at dawn. {npc} tells you about the offer at supper, between two mouthfuls of soup, as if mentioning the weather. Then {he} asks, lightly: "Did you ever wonder if I would take it?"

effects.log: "Never," you say. {npc} smiles into {his} soup. That was the right answer, and it was also true.
"Once," you admit. {npc} puts {his} spoon down. "Thank you for telling me," {he} says, and means it, and is hurt.

events.text: {npc} finds you alone in the corridor and does not move out of the way. "You swore a road with one of us," {he} says, "and the rest of us are only the house now. I want to know what that makes me." {His} voice is very calm. {His} hands are not.

effects.log: You tell {npc}, in plain words, what {he} is to you, which is not the road but is not less. {He} listens to every word.

choices.text: Say the vow is not for discussion

effects.log: "The vow is the vow," you say. {npc} steps aside. The house is very cold for a month.

events.text: {npc} has started training at dawn, hard, alone, in the far courtyard, where you cannot help seeing. It takes you a week to understand. {He} is not trying to be stronger. {He} is trying to be chosen. When you come into the courtyard, {npc} stops and waits, sword lowered.

effects.log: You spar until the sun is high. You say nothing about vows. Afterwards {npc} laughs for the first time in a month.
"You are hurting yourself," you say. "Yes," says {npc}. "I noticed that too." {He} does not stop.

events.text: You have gone two realms past {npc} now, and it shows in everything: {he} cannot follow your sparring, cannot feel the qi you speak of, sits in on your seclusions like a guest at someone else's prayer. One night {he} says it first. "You can go on without me. I will not hold it against you."

effects.log: "I swore to wait," you say. "I will." {npc} cries, then, for the first time in your marriage, quietly, into your shoulder.
You do not answer that night. Both of you lie awake listening to the other not sleep.

events.text: {npc} is two realms ahead of you now. {He} slows when you walk together, shortens {his} stride, pretends not to feel the weather that only {his} realm can feel. You see the effort. It is kinder than anything {he} could say, and it is unbearable.

effects.log: "Go at your own pace," you say. "I will catch up." {npc} looks at you a long time and lengthens {his} stride, a little.
You train at night, alone, until your hands bleed. {npc} finds the bandages and says nothing about them.

events.text: One morning you stand beside {npc} at the edge of the training ground and feel the same weather {he} feels, the same faint pull of the next stair. Neither of you is ahead. Neither of you says anything about it. {npc} just hands you your sword, the way {he} used to, before.

effects.log: You train together until noon, and it is exactly like before, and better.
"I did not wait," {npc} says. "I walked slowly. That is different." You decide it is not, and say so.

events.text: You hand {npc} back the half of the incense stick you swore on, or {he} hands you yours; afterwards neither of you can remember which. The marriage stands. The road does not. {npc} says only: "I hope the top is worth getting to alone."

mem.note: was told the top was worth it

effects.log: You say it. It is the truest thing either of you has said in months, and the coldest.

mem.note: got no answer at the end of the road

effects.log: You say nothing. {npc} nods as if you had, and goes inside.

events.text: {dcp_name} is gone. The vow does not say what to do now; the old books are silent on it, as if nobody who swore it ever lived long enough to ask. You find the half of the incense stick in a drawer, still with the ash on it, and you sit holding it until the light goes.

choices.text: Walk the road alone, for both

effects.log: You will walk it for both of you, then. Every step from now on counts double, or it does not count at all.
You bury it in the grave. The vow goes where {dcp_name} went. You will have to find your own reasons now.

events.text: The white stairs came down for {dcp_name}, and {dcp_name} climbed them, and looked back at you once from the first step. Now there is an empty side of the bed and an empty seat at the training ground, and somewhere above the clouds, someone is waiting for you to keep your half of the vow.

effects.log: You train until you cannot stand. Then you get up and train some more. The clouds are not going to come to you.

choices.text: Look up for a long time

effects.log: You stand in the courtyard and look up until your neck aches. Somewhere up there. Waiting. You will not be long.

events.text: Up here, a year is nothing; a decade is a long afternoon. Below, {dcp_name} is still climbing. You keep a seat for them at the edge of the jade terrace, and every so often you part the clouds and look down, though you know you will not find them, and come back and sit.

effects.log: You keep it. The other immortals have learned not to sit in it. One of them leaves a cup of tea there, now and then.
You send a dream down through the clouds: a stair, a terrace, a seat. Whether it arrives, you cannot know.

events.text: An immortal of the Jade Court asks you, kindly, why you never take a new companion up here, where there are so many who would. You try to explain about {dcp_name}, and a vow, and the white stairs, and find you have been talking for an hour. The immortal has stopped asking and started listening.

effects.log: You finish it. The immortal bows to you, deeply, and goes away, and does not ask again.
You stop and laugh. "It is a long road," you say. "I am only halfway through telling it."

events.text: {npc} is at the top of the white stairs, exactly where the vow said {he} would be. {He} has kept a seat for you at the edge of the cloud terrace, and the cup on it is still warm, as if {he} had known the hour. "You were long," {npc} says. "I did say not to be long."

effects.log: You sit. The clouds go gold beneath you. Neither of you says anything for a very long time, and nothing needs to be said.
"I am here now," you say. "Then we can begin," says {npc}, "the next part of the road."

events.text: You waited above the clouds so long that waiting became a kind of cultivation, and now {npc} comes up the white stairs, out of breath, older and somehow younger, and stops two steps below you as if not quite sure you are real. You hold out your hand, the way you did once on a ledge above a gorge.

effects.log: You pull {npc} up the last two steps. "You kept the seat," {he} says. "I kept the seat," you agree.
You let {npc} climb the last two by {his} own strength, because that was the vow too. {He} reaches the top laughing.
